n: A wise woman builds up her household—her family and home—while a foolish one tears it down with her own hands. Homes are built or ruined by daily choices.
How we live shows what we think of God. An upright life shows reverence; a crooked life shows contempt.
A fool’s proud talk becomes a rod that strikes back at him; the words of the wise protect them.

f.g: Proud words that become a whip for his own back.

n: A practical farmer’s proverb: without oxen the stall stays clean, but you also get no big harvest. Productive work is messy, but worth it.
An honest witness doesn’t lie; a false witness pours out lies.

f.w: A faithful witness will not lie

n: A mocker searches for wisdom and finds none, because his attitude blocks it. To the humble, knowledge comes easily.

f.w: A scorner seeketh wisdom, and findeth it not

n: Walk away from a fool when you notice his words have no knowledge in them.

f.w: Go from the presence of a foolish man

n: Wisdom helps a person understand where he is going; the folly of fools is self-deception.
Fools mock at making amends for sin, but among the upright there is goodwill.

f.w: Fools make a mock at sin
f.g: Possibly “fools mock the guilt offering”—they scorn making amends.

n: Each heart knows its own deepest sorrow and joy; no one else can fully share them. Only Christ fully understands our inner experience.

f.w: The heart knoweth his own bitterness

f.g: intermeddle = share in, take part in.

n: A wicked person’s solid house will fall, but even the tent of the upright will thrive.
A sobering warning: a road can look right but end in death. Our own judgment needs God’s guidance. This saying repeats in 16:25.

f.w: There is a way which seemeth right unto a man

n: Laughter can hide a heavy heart, and joy may end in grief. Outward cheer doesn’t always reflect inner life.
The faithless will get their fill of their own ways, and good people will be rewarded for theirs.

f.g: backslider = one who turns away from the right path.

n: The naive believe anything they hear; prudent people think about where they are going.
The wise are cautious and steer clear of evil; fools are reckless and overconfident.
A quick-tempered person acts foolishly, and a scheming person is hated.
The naive end up with folly as their inheritance; the prudent are crowned with knowledge.
In the end, evil people will bow before the good and beg at the gates of the righteous, as Joseph’s brothers bowed to him.

f.w: The evil bow before the good

n: A sad observation: the poor are shunned even by neighbors, while the rich have plenty of “friends.”
Looking down on a neighbor is sin; being kind to the needy brings happiness. Verse 20 describes; this verse commands.

f.w: he that hath mercy on the poor, happy is he

n: Those who plot evil go astray, but those who plan good find love and faithfulness.

f.g: Steadfast love and faithfulness (ḥesed and ʾemet).

n: All hard work brings a profit, but mere talk leads only to poverty.
Wealth is a crown for the wise; folly is the only “crown” fools receive.
A truthful witness can save lives in court; a false one only deceives.

f.g: Saves lives—in a trial, honest testimony can save an innocent person.

n: Reverence for the Lord gives a secure fortress, and his children will have refuge.
Reverence for the Lord is a life-giving spring that helps one avoid death’s traps. Compare 13:14, where the same is said of wise teaching.
A king’s glory is in having many people; a ruler without subjects is ruined. Leaders are only as strong as the people they serve.
Patience shows great understanding; a hot temper shows off foolishness.

f.w: He that is slow to wrath

n: A peaceful heart gives life to the body, but envy rots the bones. Our inner state affects our physical health.

f.w: envy the rottenness of the bones

n: Oppressing the poor insults their Creator, because they are made in his image. Kindness to the needy honors God.
The wicked are brought down by their own evil, but the righteous find refuge even in death.

f.w: the righteous hath hope in his death

n: Wisdom rests quietly in a discerning heart; even among fools it makes itself known.

f.g: Settles in, makes itself at home.

n: Righteousness lifts a nation up; sin brings disgrace on any people. The Book of Mormon shows this pattern again and again.
A king favors a wise servant but is angry with one who acts shamefully.
